A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAAR research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching reorganized material.

before.justification: v2 reports original controlled data-selection and LLM fine-tuning experiments, benchmark comparisons and ablations in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendices F–H.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds labeling, embedding-efficiency, pipeline-stability, model-scale and seed-injection experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains centroid synthesis, pseudo-label clustering, two-stage MLP training on frozen LLM representations and selection by predicted entropy. The newly tested component variants are ablations; they do not replace the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Dolly-15K, Cot-en, Math-Instruct and Code-Alpaca pool, the same seven downstream benchmarks and MMLU. The additions vary model configurations and method components within this retained data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 14 adds GTE-Qwen2-7B and Qwen3-8B-Embedding as embedding-extraction cost comparators against the native embedding layer. The original data-selection baseline set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Llama3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-14B configurations, controlled label and seed-injection variants, and embedding timing on 40K samples. The original benchmark subsets, metrics, LoRA settings and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices F.4–F.5 and G.7–G.8 test pseudo-labels versus ground-truth labels, internal versus external embeddings, full-pipeline stability, model scale and downstream seed injection. These substantially expand validation of the design. The earlier entropy-versus-diversity ablation is retained as F.6.

E5.justification: v3 adds a three-run Qwen2-7B study with individual results, means and standard deviations in Table 17. Its checklist also clarifies averaging over two seeds for the main experiments, whose stated two repetitions remain unchanged. Formal significance tests are not specified.

E6.justification: The original benchmark scores are retained, but substantial new results are reported. Table 23 adds DAAR averages of 61.54 versus Random's 60.80 on Qwen2.5-14B and 29.64 versus 29.52 on Llama3.2-3B. Other new tables report labeling effects, embedding costs, run variability and seed-removal outcomes.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.2 defines deterministic-assignment approximation error and adds Proposition C.1, Equation (15), and entropy-related reasoning. This is a limited mathematical extension; the existing importance-weight decomposition and its derivation are retained, with the latter moved from Appendix E to C.1.

C1.justification: The introduction withdraws the asserted proof that optimal selection must maximize mutual information, replacing it with an importance-sampling rationale for effective diversity selection. The corresponding contribution bullet changes, while the abstract and principal methodological and empirical claims remain.

C2.justification: New discussions interpret ground-truth labels as potentially misaligned with model representations, low run variability as evidence against compounding errors, and seed injection as accelerating generation with little effect on accuracy. Appendix C.2 additionally links entropy to approximation error, substantially extending the mechanistic interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix G.8 newly states that downstream samples used for seeding are disjoint from final evaluation datasets. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed split. Existing prompts, hyperparameters, software, hardware and public code information are largely retained and relocated.

R1.justification: Related work explicitly extends its diversity discussion to pre-training and adds works including Aioli, RegMix, Dynamic Gradient Alignment and Chameleon. Additional citations appear elsewhere, but the positioning between data selection and data mixing remains broadly unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized to place implementation and theory before experimental setup and baselines, with a detailed contents list replacing the overview. v3 also adds a NeurIPS checklist and acknowledgments and revises explanatory passages, while retaining much of the main narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds numerous tables for robustness, stability, model scale and seed injection, including a main-text ground-truth-label comparison. Figure 3 redraws existing centroid heatmaps while the appendix version remains. Figures and tables are extensively reflowed, with several captions shortened.

improvement.justification: The added ablations, seed/evaluation separation disclosure and three-run uncertainty estimates make the empirical evidence easier to assess, while the introduction narrows an unsupported optimality claim. These gains are tempered by new overstatements: C.2's Equation (15) permits zero error at positive entropy when domain weights are equal, and Table 25 claims statistical insignificance without specifying a test.
